text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- Agriculture Minister Wilhelm Molterer plans stricter rules on the planting of genetically manipulated plants. However, he sees a danger in taking the issue emotionally.
- Transport Minister Caspar Einem wants to lower the maximum blood-alcohol level for drivers to 0.05 percent.
- Wintisa chief Franz Fuchs sees eastern European countries as an example for Austria's planned reform of the public pension system.
- Austria's under-16s football team won the second place in the European CHapionships in Germany at the weekend, after having lost the final against Spain through penalty kicks.
- Austria's constitutional judges criticise the government for making constitutional changes without the approval of the constitutional court.
- Austrian firms have invested more than 40 billion schillings in over 14,000 companies in eastern Europe.
- The conservative People's Party's general secretary Othmar Karas demands Bank Austria shouldt be privatised as quickly as possible in order to reduce political influence in the banking sector.

- Helmut Frisch, head of the state deficit committee, says it would be a "catastrophe" should Austria not take part in the European Economic and Monetary Union. Austria's schilling could not be kept stable in such a case.

- Justice Minister Michalek will present first reports on the affair concerning the government's involvement in the flight of the suspected Iranian murderers of three Kurdish leaders in 1989. Second Parliamentary President conservative Heinrich Neisser wants a parliamentary investigation in the case.
- Electronics retailer Koeck plans to expand into the photography business.
- Bank Austria plans to stop risk financing of building projects.

- Conservatives criticise Social Democrat Transport Minister Caspar Einem's draft telecommunications law. They say it is too protective of the current monopoly Post&Telekom Austria and provides too little competition.
- Economics Minister Hannes Farnleitner wants Austria's electricity companies to work together more closely in a bid to prepare for the liberalisation of the market.
